Proposal — dedupe both tied PATH interfaces before startup prepends, then force Homebrew bin first after the last one:

In `~/.config/zsh/zshrc`, at the top of the PATH section, before `brew shellenv`:

```zsh
typeset -U PATH path
```

`-U` applies only to the name being assigned. `brew shellenv`, `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`, and the grok installer all assign scalar `PATH`, so both interfaces need the flag. Repeat prepends of a directory already in PATH are then dropped instead of growing PATH.

That does not keep Homebrew first. `.local/bin` is prepended after `brew shellenv`, and `~/.zshrc` prepends `$HOME/.grok/bin` after the `source` returns. With `-U`, an existing directory stays at its first position, so those writes outrank `/opt/homebrew/bin`.

At the end of `~/.zshrc`, after the grok `PATH` line:

```zsh
path=(/opt/homebrew/bin ${path:#/opt/homebrew/bin})
```

`${path:#/opt/homebrew/bin}` removes every existing copy, and the assignment puts that directory first exactly once. After `source ~/.zshrc`, PATH is the same length and `/opt/homebrew/bin` is first.
